title: Dangling generation curator and client flow-control strategy
creator: Maya Patel
description: Summary: Client disconnects, transient network flaps, and long-running generations leave behind partial output blobs, KV-prefix entries, and lease state that inflate resource usage and can lead to stale model state being served to resumed sessions. This ticket proposes a "curator" pattern plus flow-control policy to reliably reclaim 'dangling' generations while enabling resume where possible and maintaining compatibility with older SDKs.
problem_statement: We observe three failure modes: 1) Abrupt client disconnects with no resume token leading to orphaned generation objects and KV cache entries; 2) Clients with intermittent connectivity repeatedly reattach and create duplicate partial generations, confusing backpressure logic and increasing token costs; 3) Older SDKs without resume-token support rely on heuristics and are currently incompatible with proposed lease semantics. Current cleanup is ad-hoc and not bounded in time, causing increased memory/GPU KV footprint and billing anomalies for customers.
proposed_solution_overview: Implement a lightweight 'curatord' sidecar process in the serving plane to own lifecycle decisions for partial generations, combined with: 1) lease-based session fingerprints and generation nonces; 2) a configurable delayed-ack window with heartbeat/keepalive; 3) compact-on-orphan policy (tiered TTL and compaction); 4) a compatibility shim for SDKs that lack resume-token support. The curator coordinates reclamation, issues tombstones for KV prefixes, and offers a salvage handshake for resumed clients.
technical_details: Session fingerprint: stable 128-bit hash derived from customer-id + API-key-hash + connection-epoch; renewed on explicit resume. Not persisted beyond metadata store TTL.
Lease tokens: short-lived (default 60s) opaque tokens granted per-active-generation. Lease renewal requires heartbeats or explicit resume; curator can forcibly revoke on policy violation.

Delayed-ack window: default 45s after client 'disconnect' event we keep partial output and allow resume. After 45s curator marks generation as 'detached' and emits a salvage token. Salvage window default 5m for resume with replay toleration. After salvage window compaction begins.

Compaction policy: two-phase. Phase 1 (detached -> tombstone): drop ephemeral KV prefixes; persist minimal checkpoint metadata to allow 'best-effort' resume. Phase 2 (tombstone -> delete): full blob compaction after default 1h if no resume occurs. Configurable per-customer/route.

Compatibility shim: for SDKs without resume-token, accept a 'heuristic-resume' mode where client-reconnect within 30s uses session fingerprint + reconnection nonce to map to recent detached generation. This is Opt-In per API key due to safety and fraud risk.
backpressure_changes: Per-client token bucket that tracks inflight token allocation instead of global per-connection quota to reduce duplicate allocations on flapping connections.
On reconnect that claims the same session fingerprint, curator will reconcile duplicate inflight allocations and reassign remaining budget to the newest connection to avoid double-billing.
Integrate with existing lease-based ownership (ENG-44610) but add curator-first arbitration to avoid split-brain allocation when multiple frontends attempt to resume the same generation.
acceptance_criteria: Curatord deployed to canary (1% traffic) and correctly transitions generations through Detached -> Tombstone -> Deleted states per policy.
Reconnect/resume flow works end-to-end for modern SDKs using resume-token: resumed generation continues from last acknowledged token and KV prefix is intact.
Heuristic-resume mode for legacy SDKs successfully reattaches to recent detached generations within 30s in 90% of test cases and is gated behind per-key opt-in.
No regression in latency p50/p95 for streaming requests beyond 5% in canary traffic.
Metrics: orphaned-generation-count drops by >=90% in canary compared to baseline after compaction window elapses.
Security review completed for salvage tokens and heuristic-resume mode (see design doc).
rollout_plan: Phase A: implement curatord and lease token flow; unit & integration tests; internal deploy to staging.
Phase B: Canary (1%): enable for low-risk customers and internal tests; collect metrics; 48h observation window.
Phase C: Gradual ramp: 1% -> 10% -> 50% over 2 weeks if metrics good; enable compatibility shim only for opt-in API keys.
Phase D: Full rollout + expose per-tenant config in Console under runtime-1.24 release notes.
monitoring_and_alerting: New SLI: orphaned_generations_reclaimed.rate >= 0.9 over 1h after compaction window.
Alert: orphaned_generations.count > 1000 for any single tenant for >15m -> P0 paging.
Dashboard: per-route delayed-ack window heatmap and median salvage-latency.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Heuristic-resume improves UX for older SDKs but increases risk of resuming wrong session; therefore opt-in only.

Keeping delayed-ack window too long increases resource usage and attack surface for forged salvage tokens; too short reduces resume success rate. Proposed defaults are a pragmatic middle-ground (45s/5m/1h) based on observed reconnection patterns.
Curatord introduces an additional control plane component in runtime; to mitigate coupling we will implement it as a sidecar process per serving pool with minimal dependencies.
